# Next.js Turbopack

Curated by Skill Harbor: practical guidance for Next.js 16 and later, where Turbopack is the default development bundler. Turbopack is an incremental bundler written in Rust that makes dev startup and hot module replacement much faster, especially on large apps, with filesystem caching that makes restarts dramatically quicker. The skill covers when to stay on Turbopack for day-to-day development, when to fall back to webpack (only if you hit a Turbopack bug or depend on a webpack-only plugin in dev), how production builds behave depending on your Next.js version, and the small but breaking rename from middleware.ts to proxy.ts. Also useful for diagnosing slow dev startup or sluggish hot reload and for reviewing bundler choices. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; written for Next.js 16+, so check the official Next.js docs for your version because defaults and flags differ between releases. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
